generationProcedure: Start from the frozen, reviewed tree; no uncommitted source change.
Run npm run build:design-system-preview to serve the internal catalogue.

Write baselines only on that reviewed tree with npx playwright test -c playwright.design-system.config.ts --update-snapshots; this is an explicit, reviewed action, never a way to make a failing test green.
Commit the PNGs together with the reviewed change.
Run acceptance on every later verification WITHOUT --update-snapshots: npx playwright test -c playwright.design-system.config.ts.

If a comparison fails, classify the diff as intended change, rendering-environment change or regression before any regeneration; an environment change needs a new platform suffix, never a silent overwrite.

nonSelfValidatingCaveat: A baseline generated in the same run that compares it cannot prove the implementation correct. The 26 PNGs record the visual state of the frozen tree; they are evidence for a future comparison, not an approval. A passing comparison proves only that pixels did not change.
knownLimitations: Chromium/Windows-specific; Firefox, WebKit, macOS, Linux, real phones and high-DPI hardware are not covered.
The baselines are self-generated evidence; a later run without --update-snapshots is the acceptance comparison, and the independent reviewer must reproduce it.
Only the stated galleries/widths/modes are captured; not every component state or consumer composition.
A visual pass is not accessibility conformance, brand approval or publication authorisation.
Screenshots are page captures anchored to the gallery top, not full-page captures.

The earlier claim that 26 committed PNGs were generated with --update-snapshots as the recorded acceptance command is removed: writing snapshots is an explicit baseline-generation step, and acceptance never uses --update-snapshots.

Third-round correction (2026-11-03): the two 320x812 instrument captures were deliberately refreshed after the committed baselines no longer matched the same Chromium/Windows renderer. The refreshed images were compared with the previous ones: identical layout and content, pixel differences confined to text antialiasing (mean absolute delta ~1.2/255, bbox across the text area). The other 24 baselines are byte-identical to the delivery candidate. This is a renderer-environment refresh, not a design change; a later environment change must use a new platform suffix, never a silent overwrite.
